rules.semantic: A kit setting its state bits from Lua goes through the real hide rule: flipping the HIDDEN bit hides/unhides the walker (it leaves/rejoins the collision table), and a possessed body can never be hidden, so the HIDDEN bit lands only as set_hidden allowed; the other bits land as asked (narrowed to a byte).

arms.observable: hidden()==true, kit_state has HIDDEN, walker out of obmap
hidden()==false, kit_state lacks HIDDEN but keeps the other bits, still in obmap
no set_hidden call, other bits replaced

rules.function: m_hidden / m_init_fire / m_blocks_placement / og_fearless / og_line_clear / og_swap_places
rules.semantic: These Lua verbs hand back the engine's own boolean answer unchanged (hidden, attack start accepted/refused while busy, family declares blocks_placement, fearless, clear sight line, swap succeeded). The game rules live in the engine functions (walker::init_fire, og::sim::fearless (fearless.cpp:27), GameWorld::clear_sight_line, og::sim::swap_places); this row is only the true/false mapping.

rules.semantic: walker:set_hidden accepts a boolean or an integer (0 = show, nonzero = hide); anything else is a script error and changes nothing.

arms.observable: error 'walker:set_hidden: expected a boolean or 0|1', hidden() unchanged

rules.semantic: walker:alternate_cost(slot) answers the shifted alternate's price as the session sees it (a new-kit alternate costs 0 = not in play with New Specials off); a slot outside 0..NUM_SPECIALS-1 is a script error.
